identification: Ladies Omega manual-wind dress watch, c.1970s, small round yellow-metal case (almost certainly gold plated on a steel back, the usual for this type; not proven), unusual grey-on-champagne wavy striped dial (printed 'wood grain'/zebra pattern, or possibly a tiger's eye/hawk's eye stone dial) with gilt baton markers and Omega logo; script line under OMEGA reads like 'Genève' at the photo's resolution (could be De Ville). Black leather strap with gilt buckle, in a red Omega presentation box with gold logo. Catalogue says working.

viewing_check: Read the script word under OMEGA (Genève or De Ville). Open or look at the case back: steel back with 'gold plated'/'plaqué' versus a 9K/18K/750 stamp; read the calibre (e.g. 625, 620, 485) and check it runs and sets. Check under a loupe whether the dial pattern is a printed design or a stone (stone shows chatoyance as you tilt it). Check the box is the matching period Omega box.
